reason: `OrderedQueueWorker.run` swallows the exception and calls `complete_offset` in `finally` (src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:144-149), so a failed item's offset becomes committable at the next tick, contradicting the docstring at queue_consumer.py:254. The test's no-commit assertion (tests/sentry/uptime/consumers/test_results_consumer.py:1922) runs about 0.2-0.3s after submit, before the commit loop's first 1.0s wait ends (queue_consumer.py:276), after which it would commit 102; this is from reading the code, not from running the test.
